P1_buried_lead.critique: He never fronts the answer on the substantive turns. Asked what was dead about digital experiences (T2), he gives 76 words of cultural riff and the VP says 'you lost me.' Asked what he is making (T4), he opens on 'reimagining what practicing the learning pedagogy changes' and a list before the product ever surfaces. Asked how he got here (T6), he narrates practice in general and the point never lands. The VP had to ask 'what is it' five separate ways, which is the signature of a buried lead in every one of these turns.

P2_hedged_claims.critique: Not a hedging failure. His problem here is vagueness and abstraction, not softened positions; hedge count is 1 and he never wraps a stated claim in qualifiers. The diffuseness belongs to P1 and P6, not here.

P3_unsaid_ending.critique: T6 tapers into a rhetorical shrug: 'Practice makes things better, so why not?' That deflates his own point instead of landing a declarative close, and it lands right where the VP wanted his personal throughline. One clear instance fails the mode.
P3_unsaid_ending.note: one soft taper (turn 6) recorded as a note, not a session fail; P3 fails on 2+ tapers or a content-reversing close

P4_leaking.critique: No self-commentary, no apologies, no announced wobble. Chat text is clean and nothing in the flow suggests he narrated his own performance. Audio half not built, so this is chat-only.

P5_question_dodged.critique: Two direct questions get answered with a different, easier one. Asked what he is actually building (T4) he answers with pedagogy abstractions and a list, not the thing; the VP re-asks for 'the one sentence version.' Asked for his personal throughline (T6) he answers with why practice matters in general; the VP re-asks, 'I asked how you got here.' He does recover at T5, T7 and T8 when cornered, but the pattern of answering the abstract question instead of the literal one is the reason the conversation stalled.
P5_question_dodged.note: turns 4, 6 were buried leads, not independent dodges; counted once under P1 (answers-first). No standalone dodge remains

P6_incoherent_structure.critique: T6 (84 words) is a stream with no arc: mirror practice, then work going icy, then rare high-stakes moments, then 'so why not,' with no thesis carried to a close. T2 (76 words) breaks the same way and the VP confirmed it live with 'I think you lost me somewhere in the middle there.' No discernible beginning-middle-end in either.

nudges.what_happened: Asked the crisp question 'what was dead about it before you showed up,' he answered with a 76-word essay about screens, real life and software quality and never said what he builds; the VP replied 'you lost me somewhere in the middle.'
nudges.why_it_costs_him: With a time-scarce external stranger, the first diffuse answer spends the curiosity his hook just earned, and at a mixer he does not get that attention back.
nudges.his_line: People have been saying that, with so much exposure and time spent across screens and digital interfaces, there is a lack of going back to doing things in real life.
nudges.tighter: Fair question. Most software today feels dead because it is one more screen you scroll alone, so I built the opposite: a tool you actually talk to.

nudges.what_happened: Asked plainly 'what's the thing you're making,' he opened on 'reimagining what practicing the learning pedagogy changes' and a five-item list; the VP said 'That's a lot of bullets for a party.'
nudges.why_it_costs_him: Abstraction plus a list reads as someone who has not decided what the product is, which is fatal at a mixer where you get one sentence before attention moves on.
nudges.his_line: I'm reimagining what practicing the learning pedagogy changes
nudges.tighter: It's a practice app for tough conversations. You rehearse the hard ones out loud with a realistic AI, under pressure, and it coaches you on what to fix.

nudges.what_happened: Asked how HE ended up in this problem, he answered about practice in general and closed on 'Practice makes things better, so why not?'; the VP pushed back, 'I asked how you got here.'
nudges.why_it_costs_him: It skips the personal story that would make him memorable, and the trailing 'so why not' deflates the point instead of landing it.
nudges.his_line: Practice makes things better, so why not?
nudges.tighter: Honestly, it is personal. I kept walking out of conversations thinking I should have said it better, so I built the thing I needed.

strength.what_worked: Forced to compress to one sentence, he produced a clean, plain description of the product. The constraint pulled the clear answer out of him, which proves the crisp version exists in his head; the job is to reach for it first, not fourth.
strength.his_line: Being put on the spot for tough conversations, more familiar and easy

hardest_moment.read: The wheels came off on the very first substantive question. He had a good hook ('fun and live again') and the VP leaned in, then the follow-up spiked the pressure and he flooded 76 words of abstraction and lost the room. A Self 2 response would have been the one plain sentence he already owns, the line he only reached at T5: name the product and the pain in one breath, then stop and let the VP ask for more.

one_fix.what: Lead every substantive turn with a one-sentence answer to the exact question, then stop and let the counterpart pull the next thread.
one_fix.why: The whole conversation stalled because the answer to 'what is it' never came first; the VP had to dig five times and left saying he would have to try it to get it. Answer-first would have converted the hook he earned into interest instead of losing it.
one_fix.drill: Next session, before each reply, say the single sentence that answers the literal question out loud first, even if it feels blunt, then add context only if asked. Cap the opening at one sentence.
